races.name: British Stallion Studs EBF Restricted Maiden Stakes (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Chianti
runners_data.note: Lightly raced with just one run to his name — a fifth on Good ground over 5f — so the experience base is thin, though the sim-going tick is positive; style is unclassified so positional play will depend on how L Morris reads the early break.
runners_data.comment: Disappointed on debut, beaten 10l in a novice despite market support, and improvement likely on that bare form; effective at 5f. Trainer out of form at present is the concern.

runners_data.name: Fly Test
runners_data.note: Holds a recorded fade pattern across two starts on Good ground at 5f and 6f, which is a significant flag here on a quick surface over the minimum trip; Ross Coakley will need to get closer to the pace than the H tag suggests to have any chance.
runners_data.comment: Sprint-bred and at a similar level to his debut in limited starts so far, Fly Test has not found much yet but has the pedigree to progress once handicapping; nothing in the form to recommend here on current evidence.

runners_data.name: Green Titan
runners_data.note: The race's only confirmed front-runner, trained by George Boughey in decent current form (2/28 over 14 days), and Billy Loughnane's quality makes uncontested control a realistic prospect; two prior runs came on Soft so today's Good to Firm is a going step into the unknown.
runners_data.comment: Stepped up considerably from a forgettable debut to go close in a novice at Salisbury last time, beaten 2l in a performance full of promise, and Green Titan is with a trainer who has a strong strike rate here. The drop to 5f on fast ground may not be ideal for a horse who has shown his best form over 6f on soft.

runners_data.name: Articulate
runners_data.note: A debut runner with no form to assess and going tagged UNKNOWN, meaning everything about how William Pyle will position her is speculative; Kristin Frost's yard has a modest 14-day strike rate of 0/12, making it hard to project confidence.
runners_data.comment: Unraced debutant by Showcasing, a £5,000 breeze-up purchase whose dam was smart at 7f as a juvenile and is a half-brother to Perfect Spring, a fair 6f performer; the trainer is in good form. Lowest-rated in the field on our figures and hard to assess without a run.

runners_data.name: Drum Major
runners_data.note: The lowest-rated runner in the field at OR 60, carrying headgear (p) and with three runs showing progressive underperformance on Soft and Good surfaces; Lewis Edmunds takes the ride but the form string of 976 offers limited encouragement at this level.
runners_data.comment: Drum Major has shown a hint of progress back at 5f in first-time cheekpieces last time after a run of disappointing efforts over further, and sprint breeding points to the trip; the race is not strong. Still well held on form, though, and needs more to be competitive here.

runners_data.name: Kaiulani Spirit
runners_data.note: Lightly raced after a single run, finishing sixth on Soft over 5f, and the going switch to Good to Firm is an unknown quantity; Tim Easterby's yard is firing at 7/98 over 14 days which gives some handler confidence, but the style is unclassified.
runners_data.comment: Short of pace on her only start, failing to land a blow at Carlisle on debut and beaten 6l, Kaiulani Spirit rates second on our figures and needs significant improvement to feature; scope for better keeps her in the picture.

runners_data.name: South West
runners_data.note: Rob Hornby partners this hold-up type who faded in his sole start — ninth on Good ground over 6f — and the drop to 5f on quicker going does not obviously fix the fade issue; Richard Hughes's 14-day numbers are modest and this runner looks up against it tactically.
runners_data.comment: A slow start cost South West on his only outing, never competitive in a Bath maiden, but he is from a good yard, has speed in his pedigree, and is the type to improve; trainer out of form recently is a note of caution.

runners_data.name: Nasserein
runners_data.note: Twice placed fifth on Soft and Firm ground for A Watson — the same trainer as Chianti — and steps up having been close up both times; the Prominent style is a genuine fit for the likely race shape and Pierre-Louis Jamin is a strong booking at this level.
runners_data.comment: Twice fifth in limited starts, Nasserein matched his debut level at Ffos Las last time but is yet to show anything to excite here; trainer badly out of form at present is a further negative, though he is the type to do better once in handicaps.

runners_data.name: Tallahassee Lassie
runners_data.note: James Fanshawe's yard is operating at an encouraging 6/25 over 14 days, and this filly has two runs showing consistent placing in the top half of the field; the Prominent style suits the race shape well and Jack Doughty's experience is an asset at a track like Leicester.
runners_data.comment: Twice in mid-division in limited starts, sprint-bred Tallahassee Lassie has not quite built on her debut and goes in the frame on our figures at a midfield rank; a firm surface will be in her favour and there is room for improvement when handicapping, though 10l beaten last time is a stiff ask.

runners_data.name: It'sbeenemotional
runners_data.note: Two runs at Sandown over 6f in good positions (7th and 4th) suggest a horse learning its trade, and the switch to 5f on Good to Firm could sharpen the finish; N Callan is a seasoned handler and the Prominent style puts this runner in the right place if the race develops as expected.
runners_data.comment: It'sbeenemotional has not reproduced her best form over shorter trips and found the trip sharp at Lingfield last time, beaten a long way; better suited to 6f on an artificial surface, this looks a tough assignment on current evidence.

races.paceDynamic: Green Titan is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 10-runner 5f maiden and, with no other natural leader to dispute, Billy Loughnane can control the fractions from the off on Good to Firm ground at Leicester. The prominent trio of Nasserein, Tallahassee Lassie, and It'sbeenemotional will track close behind without forcing a genuinely hot pace, meaning the tempo is likely to be honest but sustainable rather than scorching. Hold-up horses Fly Test, South West, and Drum Major will be operating off a pace that may not generate enough of a furlong-and-a-half kick to pull them into contention, especially as both Fly Test and South West carry recorded fade patterns. The race shape strongly favours those who can race prominently or lead at a controlled tempo — front-running and close-tracking profiles are the primary beneficiaries on this configuration.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Green Titan Controls Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If Green Titan is allowed to stride into an uncontested lead and set a sustainable, measured pace that suits his stamina profile.
scenarios.body: If Green Titan is allowed to stride into an uncontested lead and set a sustainable, measured pace that suits his stamina profile.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Racer Runs Through
scenarios.trigger: If Green Titan's early fractions are slightly too quick for him to sustain and a prominent tracker pounces inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: If Green Titan's early fractions are slightly too quick for him to sustain and a prominent tracker pounces inside the final furlong.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closer Gets Late Run
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is quicker than expected and the field spreads, opening a clear racing line for a hold-up horse to finish strongly.
scenarios.body: If the pace is quicker than expected and the field spreads, opening a clear racing line for a hold-up horse to finish strongly.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Race Blows Wide Open
scenarios.trigger: If Green Titan misses the break or encounters trouble and the field has no clear pace-setter, causing a chaotic, muddling run.
scenarios.body: If Green Titan misses the break or encounters trouble and the field has no clear pace-setter, causing a chaotic, muddling run.

watchPoints.text: Green Titan's draw and break — if Loughnane gets away cleanly and crosses to the rail, this race is effectively over for the hold-up horses before the first furlong is complete.

Fly Test and South West both carry documented fade patterns; if either is allowed to drift into the betting on the back of hold-up market support, their in-running profile makes them poor each-way propositions at 5f on quick ground.
Nasserein runs just 8 days after his last start — monitor any market drift that could signal the stable is managing the horse rather than expecting a peak run.

The Going Report lists the 6:15 race as Good to Firm throughout multiple entries, confirming fast conditions that will stretch stamina reserves in the final furlong and could expose Green Titan's Soft-ground form base if he has set even a moderate pace.
Articulate is a debut runner for a yard with 0/12 over 14 days — watch for any significant market move, as that would be the primary signal that connections expect more than the public data suggests.

races.name: Greenhouse Sports 'Team For Life' Handicap

runners_data.name: Midnight's Dream
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse who needs a truly run race to produce his best; sim-going record of 3/15 on similar ground is modest, and recent form figures of 390006 give little confidence even in an undemanding handicap off OR 60.
runners_data.comment: Effective at 7-8f on today's going, Midnight's Dream was beaten 3l off this mark at Doncaster last time, though a tendency to be too keen hampered the effort; the settling angle remains the key if he is to show his best form here.

runners_data.name: Dancing With Drums
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front-runner; T P Queally takes the ride for the Adam Kirby yard which is firing (1/13 over 14 days), and uncontested pace on fast ground gives this horse every chance to control and outstay rivals — the STYLE_FIT tag notes it races out of its optimal role, but leading from the front is its clearest path.
runners_data.comment: Finished well beaten in eleventh on his most recent start off today's mark and needs a sharp revival after a poor run; Dancing With Drums has form over this distance but acts on good to soft and AW, and today's faster ground is an added query.

runners_data.name: Bass Player
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse wearing tongue-strap, dropping back to 7f from recent 8-10f outings; reasonable sim-going record of 8/15 but form figure of 5 in last run at 8f on Good is lukewarm, and the step back in trip may not fully suit a plodding type.
runners_data.comment: Moving in the right direction when beaten 3¼l at Nottingham last time off a slightly higher mark, Bass Player is suited to 7-8f on today's ground and first-time cheekpieces could help; winless in recent outings and our figures suggest he needs more to be competitive.

runners_data.name: Arnaz
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up operator for the Loughnane yard (1/17 over 14 days), wearing a tongue-tie and returning after 37 days off; sim-going record of 5/15 is fair on this type of surface, though 7f on fast ground and a recent string of mid-pack finishes suggest he is more place than win candidate.
runners_data.comment: Has experience of today's trip and conditions and first-time headgear could help, but Arnaz has been keen and below form in recent races; difficult to make a case on those grounds despite being rated at a fair mark over this distance.

runners_data.name: Berning Hot
runners_data.note: True hold-up racer pushed into a midfield mapping because of the congestion at the rear — M J Attwater's 4yo has genuinely solid recent form (2nd and 3rd in last five) and the 1W2P sim-going record on similar ground is a positive; the STYLE_FIT discount applies if he cannot get his natural position, but he is one of the better-credentialled hold-up types in the race.
runners_data.comment: Capable of better and effective at 7-8f on a sound surface, Berning Hot has been inconsistent and was well below form beaten 9l at Beverley last time; showing more than that is the task here.

runners_data.name: Moonhall Lass
runners_data.note: In-form 4yo for the James Owen yard which is red-hot (9/40 T14), wearing a visor; two wins in last five on Good ground and a 3rd last time out at 7f on Good are all relevant, though the sim-going record of 10/15 is spread wide and she will need to overcome the redistribution squeeze to fire from the back.
runners_data.comment: Finishing third off today's mark last time with her best work coming late, Moonhall Lass has two wins in recent form, handles the trip and ground well, and goes with a first-time visor; she is a live threat. The worry is a patchy record between her good runs.

runners_data.name: Call Glory
runners_data.note: Prominent racer for Ian Williams (3/33 T14) who has been consistently placed without winning lately — form of 342356 on Good ground at 6-7f suits the track and conditions well; one of only two genuine pace-presser types behind the leader, giving him a structurally sound pitch in this race shape.
runners_data.comment: Placed consistently earlier in his recent form but below those efforts at this course last time, Call Glory is effective at 5-7f and acts on today's going; he needs to show more than recent starts to be a factor.

runners_data.name: No Gain
runners_data.note: Prominent racer wearing a tongue-piece for the Adam Kirby yard; back-to-back placed efforts including a win at 8f on Good last time, and stepping back to 7f is the only mild query — strong recent form makes this one of the more interesting prominent profiles in the field.
runners_data.comment: Went a neck away at a higher mark last time and is in good heart, No Gain is effective from 7 to 12f on a sound surface and the application of first-time headgear adds a touch of interest; up 4lb here, which is the main question.

runners_data.name: Montpellier Green
runners_data.note: Returning after a lengthy 187-day break for Ian Williams; true hold-up type whose last five runs were all at 11-16f, making this 7f trip on fast ground a sharp drop in distance from his comfort zone — the long absence and trip reduction stack up as significant negatives, and the redistribution out of his natural position adds further difficulty.
runners_data.comment: Winless and largely out of the money in recent starts, Montpellier Green has struggled throughout this campaign across a wide range of distances and last seen well beaten; 187 days off the track since and figures rank her last in the field.

runners_data.name: Jackson Street
runners_data.note: Carries the lowest weight in the field and has 7f wins on Standard ground to his name, but recent form reads 1-2764 and the sim-going record of 3/15 on similar surfaces is weak; repositioned into midfield from his natural hold-up berth, he would need a very fortuitous run of traffic to play a role.
runners_data.comment: Doing his best work late after a slow start at Lingfield last time, Jackson Street has won in recent form and handles the distance and going; our figures put him below the principals and he needs to find improvement to feature.

runners_data.name: Mini Mac
runners_data.note: Wears blinkers and is the lowest-rated horse in the race (OR 52); a 2nd at 7f on Good last season shows ability on this type of surface and trip, but recent form of 608420 is uninspiring — out of natural hold-up position due to field congestion, and the stable (0/14 T14) provides little confidence.
runners_data.comment: Going well prior to finding 1m too far at Doncaster last time, beaten 5l when the trip found him out, Mini Mac is suited to 7f and the return to a shorter distance looks a clear asset; a trainer in strong form and first-time blinkers add confidence. Winless in recent starts remains the caveat.

races.paceDynamic: Dancing With Drums is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 11-runner 7f handicap on Good to Firm ground at Leicester, and with no credible challenger for the lead, T P Queally's mount should be able to control tempo without being harassed from the break. Call Glory and No Gain are the likeliest horses to push into a prominent position behind the leader, giving the race a clear shape: a single pace-setter, two chasers in behind, and a large cluster of hold-up types scrambling for ground in the back half. This structure strongly favours runners who can sit close to the pace without burning energy fighting for position — prominent-to-midfield racers who can track the steady, uncontested gallop and pounce in the final two furlongs on fast ground will be ideally placed. This field contains far more true hold-up types than the map can accommodate at the rear — Berning Hot, Moonhall Lass, Montpellier Green, Jackson Street, and Mini Mac are all genuine come-from-behind horses who will be competing for space and may not achieve their natural position, with Moonhall Lass and Berning Hot — both in form — the most likely to secure a workable pitch given their class edge over the group.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Front Rewards
scenarios.trigger: If Dancing With Drums bowls along unchallenged at a comfortable pace and the hold-up pack fails to close from the rear.
scenarios.body: If Dancing With Drums bowls along unchallenged at a comfortable pace and the hold-up pack fails to close from the rear.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Swamp Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Call Glory or No Gain press Dancing With Drums into a stronger-than-expected gallop and the leader is overhauled in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: If Call Glory or No Gain press Dancing With Drums into a stronger-than-expected gallop and the leader is overhauled in the final furlong.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Late Surge
scenarios.trigger: If Dancing With Drums sets too strong a pace early and the race truly falls apart in the straight, opening a late lane.
scenarios.body: If Dancing With Drums sets too strong a pace early and the race truly falls apart in the straight, opening a late lane.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsider Capitalises on Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If the pack of repositioned hold-up types disrupt each other mid-race and a lightly-regarded runner finds a clear run at the right moment.
scenarios.body: If the pack of repositioned hold-up types disrupt each other mid-race and a lightly-regarded runner finds a clear run at the right moment.

watchPoints.text: Dancing With Drums holds the race by the throat from the front — if T P Queally controls fractions with no pressure, the race could be over as a contest turning for home; watch whether Call Glory or No Gain push close enough to ensure a true gallop.

Moonhall Lass and Berning Hot are both natural closers squeezed into a midfield draw on the map — watch how cleanly Billy Loughnane and L Morris can find their natural positions at the back of the field without getting shuffled back too far on a course where fast-ground 7f can be unforgiving late.

Montpellier Green is returning from 187 days off and drops sharply in trip from 11-16f to 7f — if he shows any signs of greenness or sluggishness early, he could prove a hazard in the pack of hold-up types bunched together mid-race.

No Gain is equipped with a tongue-piece and has won over a longer trip on Good ground — watch whether Charles Bishop elects to push forward to press Dancing With Drums or settles for a tracking position, as that tactical call will define which scenario unfolds.

The going is reported Good to Firm at Leicester for this 7f contest despite the card header showing Good — fast ground favours prominent racers who don't need the race truly strung out, reinforcing the front-biased shape.

races.name: Global Harvester Handicap

runners_data.name: Pisanello
runners_data.note: Veteran hold-up performer at nine years old, whose sim-going record (7 runs, no wins, one place on similar) offers limited encouragement; D O'Meara's runner has been racing over shorter distances recently and the step back up to 1m4f is a requirement rather than an obvious plus — genuine closer who will be forced to race closer than ideal given the field makeup.
runners_data.comment: Held to form last time, going down by just 2l off a mark 2lb higher than today's, and Pisanello is well suited to 8-10f on any going; a hold-up style should allow him to pick off rivals late in a 12f contest, and the mark looks workable. Without a win in recent starts is the straightforward caveat.

runners_data.name: Ottoman
runners_data.note: Billy Loughnane takes over on this four-year-old who has placed five times on similar going, including a recent third over 1m4f at Goodfield; headgear noted and a hold-up type who brings a credible sim-going record (11 runs, one win, five places) — the natural style is rear-of-field but the bunched midfield is where he'll end up.
runners_data.comment: Returned to form with a 5l third in a handicap on his most recent start, Ottoman has found his conditions here in 10-12f on a sound surface and the first-time cheekpieces could extract more; he is interesting if he reproduces that effort. Yet to win in recent starts is the concern.

runners_data.name: Pureis King
runners_data.note: Won last time out over 1m2f on good ground and filled the runner-up spot the time before, giving this A W Carroll charge the best recent winning form in the race; carries a fades-in-finish flag which is worth monitoring, having returned over 1m4f now, but the quick turnaround (just 2 days) is noted and Callum Hutchinson keeps the ride.
runners_data.comment: Landing a classified race at Ffos Las by 4l just two days ago in a manner that left something in reserve, Pureis King arrives here in excellent form; effective at 10f on good ground and top of our rankings. A quick turnaround and penalty are the only reservations against a horse clearly in his best form.

runners_data.name: Clipsham Noble
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front-runner, rated OR 50 and shaped by the pace map as the race's sole pace source; won over 1m4f on good ground in good style earlier and the 31-day break is the main query — if fresh and sound, dictating a controlled pace at this level is well within reach, though the style-fit flag reflects this field context rather than any fundamental concern about the horse itself.
runners_data.comment: Landed a handicap here last time off a mark 4lb lower, overcoming a slow start to assert with something to spare, and Clipsham Noble stays a broad range from 8 to 12f on a variety of surfaces; a trainer in good form adds confidence. Up 4lb now so the task is slightly tougher, and he usually needs to come from behind.

runners_data.name: Abila
runners_data.note: Ian Williams runner who has struggled to land a blow in six handicap starts, all on standard/slow ground at tracks including Kempton and Carlisle; the sim-going record (1 from 6, no wins, no places on similar) is the weakest in the race and this genuinely hold-up performer is squeezed to midfield by the redistribution — hard to make a case.
runners_data.comment: Consistently held in recent outings and without a credible performance in UK company, Abila has experience of today's distance and going; she seemed suited by longer trips in France, but was comfortably beaten last time here and the figures offer little encouragement.

runners_data.name: Myna
runners_data.note: The most consistent horse in the field by recent form, with four finishes between first and fourth in her last six outings including a win over 1m2f on good ground; Myla Coppins rides and the A W Carroll yard have been firing in at 11/60 over 14 days — though her natural rear-of-field style places her in midfield here, she is among the most likely of the redistributed group to mount a genuine challenge.
runners_data.comment: Fourth in a classified race at Lingfield last time, holding a consistent level, Myna has won in recent form and handles today's going; first-time hood is a talking point and she is capable of a similar showing. Without a win for a while suggests she may face a tough task at the top end.

runners_data.name: Majestic Leo
runners_data.note: Carries both a fades-in-finish flag and a career form line (060890) that reads of limited confidence at this level; the sim-going record (6 runs, no wins, no places) matches the disappointing form and the horse must come from a midfield berth having been displaced from its natural hold-up position — trainer G Brown has drawn a blank in his two 14-day runners.
runners_data.comment: Out of form throughout recent starts and failing to land a blow down the field at Windsor most recently, Majestic Leo faces an uphill task; first-time headgear applied and handles today's conditions, but needs to find significant improvement to figure.

runners_data.name: Duke Orsino
runners_data.note: Jenkins-trained four-year-old who placed twice over 1m2f and 1m1f on good ground earlier in the season but has been running on all-weather since and steps back up sharply in trip; displaced into midfield from its natural hold-up berth and the sim-going (5 from 13, no wins, no places) does not compel — trip and surface switch are positives but form trajectory is a concern.
runners_data.comment: Despite rearing at the start last time, Duke Orsino kept on for fourth at Lingfield, doing well to finish as close as he did in the circumstances; handles today's going and is effective at 7-10f. An exposed maiden profile and weak recent form make him hard to enthuse about.

runners_data.name: Coverbridge
runners_data.note: P Winks representative who placed fourth over 1m4f on good ground last time, showing the trip is not an issue; the sim-going record (8 runs, no wins, no places) is modest but the recent handicap form over the right distance has some shape to it — a natural hold-up type reassigned to midfield, and Ben Ffrench-Davis takes the ride for the small Winks yard.
runners_data.comment: The return to a longer trip should help Coverbridge, who was below her best at a shorter trip last time; effective from 7 to 12f on a range of surfaces. Without a win in recent form and lowest-ranked on our figures, she needs everything to fall right.

races.paceDynamic: Clipsham Noble is the sole confirmed front-runner in this nine-runner 1m4f handicap and, with no rival likely to press hard for the lead, will dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the outset on good to firm ground at Leicester. The field is saturated with hold-up types — Myna, Abila, Duke Orsino, Coverbridge, Majestic Leo and Pisanello all want to come from off the pace — meaning a significant portion of the field cannot secure their natural position and will race closer than ideal. Of those redistributed hold-up horses, Myna and Pureis King carry the best recent form and are most likely to edge into the more prominent midfield berths, while the remainder settle into a bunched chasing pack. With a lone leader setting a measured tempo over this trip on fast ground, the race shape strongly favours horses who can travel prominently in behind Clipsham Noble and produce a sustained run from two furlongs out — late closers dependent on a truly run race face the prospect of not enough pace to exploit.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Clipsham Noble Leads Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If Clipsham Noble breaks well and controls the tempo unchallenged at a steady-to-fair pace, this shape plays out as a procession from the front.
scenarios.body: If Clipsham Noble breaks well and controls the tempo unchallenged at a steady-to-fair pace, this shape plays out as a procession from the front.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Stalkers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Clipsham Noble is tracked closely by Myna or Pureis King and the leaders quicken early in the straight, the race resolves between the top two or three.
scenarios.body: If Clipsham Noble is tracked closely by Myna or Pureis King and the leaders quicken early in the straight, the race resolves between the top two or three.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Deliver Late
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is unexpectedly strong enough to string the field out and create a true end-to-end gallop, hold-up horses from the redistributed group land a late blow.
scenarios.body: If the early pace is unexpectedly strong enough to string the field out and create a true end-to-end gallop, hold-up horses from the redistributed group land a late blow.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Breaks It Wide Open
scenarios.trigger: If Clipsham Noble is taken on unexpectedly early or loses its action, the race degenerates into a chaotic sprint finish that scrambles the order.
scenarios.body: If Clipsham Noble is taken on unexpectedly early or loses its action, the race degenerates into a chaotic sprint finish that scrambles the order.

watchPoints.text: Clipsham Noble's price in-running — if it quickens clear turning into the straight with no pressure, the race may already be over for anything held up deep.

Myna's position at the break: if Myla Coppins can secure a prominent midfield berth rather than being trapped wide or deep, it becomes the most dangerous threat to Clipsham Noble given the consistent recent form.
Pureis King's fades-in-finish flag is significant at 1m4f — watch whether it travels strongly to the two-furlong pole; if it hits the front too soon given that flag, it may not see out the trip.

The bunched hold-up group (Abila, Duke Orsino, Coverbridge, Ottoman, Pisanello) risk a scrimmage leaving the back straight — any traffic trouble through the pack at the three-furlong mark could cost several horses their chance simultaneously.

Going is described as Good To Firm for this race despite the headline race card showing Good — fast ground and a steady pace set by one front-runner will test stamina reserves of any horse who does not travel kindly.

races.name: Samworth Brothers Handicap

runners_data.name: Over Spiced
runners_data.note: The form string (215543) shows consistent involvement in finishes and the sim-going record (12/15, 2W7P) demonstrates effectiveness on good ground — a horse that arrives here fit off 13 days and drops deeper in the field than ideal, but has the class and recent course-condition form to be competitive if the pace is genuine.
runners_data.comment: Third last time at this mark, Over Spiced is consistent and at home over 5f on a sound surface; the first-time cheekpieces from draw 3 add interest. Still 2lb above her last winning mark, which is the one caveat to an otherwise solid profile.

runners_data.name: The Coffee Pod
runners_data.note: Returns from a 73-day break for Muir & Grassick, and that layoff is the primary concern; sim-going figures are modest (8/15, 0W2P) and recent form is weak, meaning even a good draw and a race run to suit could be insufficient to offset the fitness question.
runners_data.comment: Winless in recent starts but The Coffee Pod tops the field on our figures, rated 76, and drops back to the 5f trip that suits best with any ground workable. First-time hood could help the settling issues that hampered her over longer last time; the 73-day gap is the main query.

runners_data.name: Startling
runners_data.note: The sole confirmed pace-setter in this field, Loughnane can dictate entirely on his terms; the STYLE_FIT flag (0.93) is worth noting — Startling is shown as Prominent but its natural lead role is confirmed, and on good to firm Leicester ground over 5f an uncontested lead is a significant tactical asset even if class queries remain.
runners_data.comment: Kept to a consistent level, finishing a close second at Southwell just a week ago off this same mark, Startling is well placed on ground and trip she handles, and a trainer in strong form adds appeal. Still without a win in recent starts, though that run confirms she has the ability.

runners_data.name: Bibendum
runners_data.note: Recent form (3-0450) is uninspiring and the headgear entry (hg:v) suggests Camacho is searching for a key; by nature a true hold-up horse pushed into a midfield berth by the race shape, its 5/15 sim-going record and modest OR of 56 make it hard to fancy even if it secures a better position than expected.
runners_data.comment: Hard to fancy off a poor recent sequence, Bibendum has failed to make the frame in latest outings and finished well beaten at Doncaster last time; the first-time visor and experience of today's conditions offer slim reasons for optimism but our figures put her well held.

runners_data.name: Bang On The Bell
runners_data.note: A seven-year-old with a creditable 1W4P sim-going record on good ground (7/15) and sound recent form including a placed effort; Jenkins' runner has been off 37 days and carries hold-up tendencies that are squeezed by this race shape, but of the redistributed closers it has the best recent placed form to suggest a finishing effort.
runners_data.comment: Showed a return to form when going down by just 2l at Nottingham last time off this same mark, and Bang On The Bell handles all conditions including today's going over this trip; first-time blinkers from draw 1 can help. The worry is a sequence without a win in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Dunnington Lad
runners_data.note: Despite a solid sim-going record (12/15) and a win at this level, the OR of 50 and recent form (U-9067) give little confidence; naturally a rear-of-field horse, the race shape forces him closer than he wants to be, and the form figures suggest he is not at his best right now.
runners_data.comment: Awful form in recent starts with finishes well down the field, and Dunnington Lad's figures place him at the foot of this market; a willingness to get on with it from the front is the one genuine positive, but there is precious little else to commend him here.

races.paceDynamic: Startling is the sole confirmed front-runner in this six-runner 5f handicap and, with no other genuine pace-pressurers to challenge him, Billy Loughnane can dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the outset on good to firm ground at Leicester. That uncontested lead is significant on a flat, quick-ground sprint: Startling can bowl along at a rhythm of his own choosing without burning energy fighting for position. The lack of early pressure means the pace is unlikely to be truly searching, which compresses the finish and typically favours horses who can travel close to the speed rather than deep closers who need a strong pace to run into. With five of the remaining six runners carrying hold-up profiles — and Bibendum, Bang On The Bell, and Dunnington Lad all genuine rear-of-field types who cannot all find their natural position in a six-runner field — the tactical verdict is clear: prominent racers and horses handy to a steady gallop are most favoured here, while true hold-up horses face a test of whether the fractions are sharp enough to reel in a front-runner who has had it entirely his own way. The field holds more hold-up types than the race shape can accommodate, with Startling virtually certain to lead and Over Spiced and The Coffee Pod the most likely to take up handy ground behind.

scenarios.body: If Startling gets a clean break and sets a controlled pace with no challenger pressuring him at any stage.

scenarios.body: If the pace proves genuinely strong enough or Startling fades, allowing the hold-up horses to finish with purpose.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Runner Pounces

scenarios.body: If a hold-up horse secures a better-than-expected pitch just off the pace and sustains a challenge from two furlongs out.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Scramble

scenarios.body: If Startling hits the front too hard early, the field bunches and a late surge from a horse with good recent form turns the race into a sprint finish.

watchPoints.text: Watch Startling's break from the stalls — if Billy Loughnane gets a clean jump and establishes the lead uncontested within the first furlong, the scenario probability shifts strongly in favour of the front-runner holding on as no rival has the natural inclination to chase.

Monitor Over Spiced's early positioning under Ashley Lewis — with five hold-up types, the horse that gets widest ground or quickest to a pitch just off Startling's heels will be best placed, and Lewis's recent trainer form (2/17 T14) adds a mild flag.

The Coffee Pod's 73-day break is a tangible fitness concern — if Lewis Edmunds is quietly positive pre-race it upgrades, but a horse returning from this layoff without a prep run in a fast-ground sprint is a risk, and the sim-going record (0W2P) offers no confidence it will run to form fresh.

Bang On The Bell and Dunnington Lad are both natural hold-up horses racing out of their comfort zone — if either appears to be tracking the pace actively in the early stages rather than dropping to the rear, it likely signals a positive ride and should be noted as a late threat.

races.name: Mark Carr Leicester Legacy Handicap

runners_data.name: Bradbury
runners_data.note: A hold-up horse in excellent recent form (two wins in last four, both over 10f on good), handled by the in-form Billy Loughnane; the step up to 1m2f from 10f looks fine based on history, and good-to-firm ground suits — best placed of the closers to exploit the steady pace by tracking from midfield.
runners_data.comment: Landed a handicap at Wetherby off a mark 10lb lower just ten days ago, showing he is in excellent form, and Bradbury stays 10f on good ground effectively; things are harder now off a higher weight but he has more to offer. First-time eye-covers could be a wildcard.

runners_data.name: Pacific Glory
runners_data.note: Drawn from a yard firing (T D Easterby 11/115 in 14 days) but running off just three career starts; a true hold-up type pushed into a midfield map position because the field is already crowded at the rear, meaning it may struggle to get the race run to suit on a track where a genuine end-to-end gallop looks unlikely.
runners_data.comment: Fourth in a maiden last time at a broadly consistent level, Pacific Glory is bred for middle-distances and may improve for handicapping; our figures put him well below the principals here, though, and he is hard to be confident about at this stage.

runners_data.name: Zooter
runners_data.note: Consistent sort with a placed effort at 10f on good going and returning fresh on just 8 days' rest; Jack Jones sends out at a modest 14-day strike-rate but the horse's form profile suggests it handles this trip and surface, and a midfield-to-closing position could be competitive if it can make ground without cover.
runners_data.comment: A genuine, free-moving stayer who goes well at this distance on a sound surface, Zooter finished a fair third two starts back before finding soft ground against him at Ffos Las most recently; back on faster ground here, the form and the mark both look right. Yet to win in recent starts is the straightforward note of caution.

runners_data.name: Fille Imbassee
runners_data.note: Headgear noted (h) and a winner over 8f on soft; the horse is a genuine hold-up type whose natural position has been pushed forward on the map by field congestion at the rear — on a day where the pace is modest, getting a clear late run from the back will be a significant ask, tempering expectations despite a useful trainer 14-day rate (1/18).
runners_data.comment: Connections have strong form at this track and Fille Imbassee has a win in recent form; at 8-9f she is proven at a similar distance, though not seeing out 10f last time here is something she needs to address. First-time hood is a talking point and she has a fair chance at a slightly lower weight.

runners_data.name: Baron Wagstaff
runners_data.note: Returning after 71 days off for R T Phillips (0/4 in 14 days), which is the longest absence in the field; a true closer whose map position understates how far back it is likely to race — limited sim-going form (1/3) adds further uncertainty, and the combination of layoff, trainer form, and redistribution makes this one of the harder to trust.
runners_data.comment: A middle-distance pedigree and the prospect of improving in handicaps are the main selling points for Baron Wagstaff, but keen tendencies have cost him and his form has been poor; 71 days off the track and below-par recent performances make him hard to recommend.

runners_data.name: Captain Cairney
runners_data.note: A natural prominent racer who is mapped to the lead because no confirmed front runner exists in this field; his style_fit (0.80) reflects that he is not an out-and-out leader by nature, but an uncontested lead on fast ground over 1m2f at Leicester gives him every chance to set a comfortable tempo and be dangerous deep into the straight — watch for him to be hard to catch if not pressed early.
runners_data.comment: Close up when runner-up here last time off today's mark, Captain Cairney produced a solid effort at this course and handles 8-10f on soft and artificial ground; first-time cheekpieces and a positive recent run give him a solid each-way profile. Acts on today's going is one uncertainty given soft and AW tend to be his best surfaces.

races.paceDynamic: Captain Cairney, a natural prominent racer redistributed to the front, is the sole pace-setter in this six-runner 1m2f handicap on good-to-firm ground at Leicester, and with no genuine front runner to push him, he will dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop throughout. The remainder of the field — Bradbury, Pacific Glory, Zooter, Fille Imbassee, and Baron Wagstaff — are all hold-up or midfield types who will track the pace at varying distances, setting up a steadily-run race with few tactical complications. Pacific Glory, Fille Imbassee, and Baron Wagstaff are true hold-up horses redistributed into midfield positions on the map because the field is saturated with closers; in reality, all three may find themselves further back than ideal, making clean ground and a strong late run harder to execute. With Captain Cairney controlling a modest pace on fast ground and no genuine pressure from behind, this race shape most strongly favours horses with tactical speed who can sit close to the action and respond when the tempo increases — a prominent or close-tracking profile has the clearest edge over pure hold-up finishers in this configuration.

watchPoints.text: Captain Cairney is unchallenged for the lead and could exploit a walking pace early — watch for Loughnane on Bradbury to position close enough to cover if Cairney kicks off a slow tempo in the straight.

Pacific Glory, Fille Imbassee, and Baron Wagstaff are all true hold-up horses crowded into midfield on the map; if they cannot find clear daylight in a small six-runner field on the far-side straight, their finishing kicks will be wasted.
Baron Wagstaff returns from 71 days off for a trainer with 0 wins from 4 in the past fortnight — fitness on reappearance is a live concern and could see it drop away when the race quickens.

Good-to-firm ground is confirmed for this 1m2f on the going report despite the listed going showing as Good — all runners appear suited to the faster surface based on sim-going profiles, but check for any late going updates that could alter the picture.

races.name: Dr T B Connors Memorial Handicap

runners_data.name: Pentonville
runners_data.note: In-form 3yo who has won two of his last three starts, trained by Boughey in excellent 14-day strike rate (4/35); runs in headgear (p), handles Good to Firm confirmed by similar-going record (1W2P), and Billy Loughnane's booking is a positive — natural hold-up profile but has scope to race prominently off a slow pace here.
runners_data.comment: Progressive and coming off back-to-back wins, Pentonville landed a handicap at Brighton last time off a mark 6lb lower, finishing strongly to score, and top course connections add further confidence; effective at 1m-10f on a sound surface. A penalty makes the task harder and he needs to handle the rise in the weights.

runners_data.name: Ritaal
runners_data.note: Muir and Grassick runner whose form string of 220-34 shows consistent placing without a win at this level; 21 days since last run is fine, but all recent runs have been on Standard (AW) which raises a mild question about turf transition to Good to Firm — hold-up style means he needs the pace to be genuine.
runners_data.comment: Produced a sound effort at Lingfield last time despite a slow start, going down by just over 3l off a slightly higher mark, and Ritaal handles 7-8f effectively; first-time cheekpieces applied here. Our figures put her below the top horses in the race and she needs more to win.

runners_data.name: Napolian
runners_data.note: The race's lone front-runner and tempo-setter, stepping up from 6f to 1m for O'Meara (7/55 in 14 days); his STYLE_FIT flag acknowledges he is stretching beyond his usual role, and his form over 6f on Good and Good to Firm is solid (0W3P) but he has never been asked to lead and sustain over this trip, which is the key unknown.
runners_data.comment: The reappearance run at Thirsk was below his best but that run can be forgiven, and Napolian has consistently been in the frame in recent starts over 6f on today's type of going; if he bounces back to form he looks a genuine danger. Second-ranked on our figures with solid placed form is a strong foundation.

runners_data.name: Station Bar
runners_data.note: Won over 8f on Firm last time out for Eve Johnson Houghton, which makes the Good to Firm conditions here theoretically suitable; a genuine deep hold-up type whose natural style cannot be served in this shape — he will need to travel closer than he'd prefer, and his STYLE_FIT flag reflects that positional compromise.
runners_data.comment: Landing a handicap at Bath by 2l last time off a mark 5lb lower, moving up through the field in good style, Station Bar handles 6-8f on good and artificial ground; the 5lb rise in the weights is the question.

runners_data.name: Venturing
runners_data.note: Returning from a 132-day absence for A W Carroll, whose 14-day record is modest (2/10); lightly raced at 3 with only three runs to go on, all on Standard or Soft, so the turf surface on Good to Firm is an unknown — as a hold-up type pushed into midfield, the layoff and ground query combine to make him risky.
runners_data.comment: Returning from a 132-day break and likely to need it, Venturing showed some ability in a maiden when fourth at Dundalk, having been supported in the market; effective at 1m on artificial ground and heavy going, which raises questions about today's fast surface.

runners_data.name: Norcross Brow
runners_data.note: 70 days off the track for Charlie Clover (1/9 in 14 days), and best effort was a second over 8f on Standard — pushed into midfield despite being a true hold-up horse, and the return from a break combined with a trainer not in strong form means he faces a steep ask to be competitive from an unnatural position.
runners_data.comment: Beaten 10l after a slow start last time, which was well below his best, Norcross Brow is effective at 7-8f on good to soft and artificial ground and comes from a trainer in strong form; off a break of 70 days he will need to bounce back sharply, but the mark is fair if he does.

runners_data.name: Albertini Star
runners_data.note: 2yo flagged as a non-runner (jockey: Non Runner) — must be treated as absent from the race; aside from that, 211 days off and a ⚠ fade-in-finish flag, plus a hold-up style redistributed to midfield, meant he carried the lowest realistic expectation of the seven even before the non-runner status.

races.paceDynamic: Napolian is the sole confirmed front-runner in a seven-runner field at Leicester's flat mile, and with no genuine rival to challenge for the lead, he is likely to control tempo from the outset at a pace entirely of his own choosing. The going report confirms Good to Firm conditions for this race, which suits a true-run mile where stamina and a clean tactical position matter. The remainder of the field — Pentonville, Ritaal, Station Bar, Venturing, Norcross Brow, and Albertini Star — are all natural hold-up or prominent types, and the field holds more hold-up horses than the race shape can accommodate at the rear; Station Bar, Norcross Brow, and Venturing are the most likely to find themselves shuffled into midfield rather than their preferred deep position. With a solo leader setting a measured, uncontested gallop, the race shape strongly favours horses who can travel prominently just off the pace and produce a sustained finish, making hold-up horses reliant on a fast enough tempo to create the gaps they need — which here looks unlikely to materialise.

watchPoints.text: Napolian's stamina over 1m is completely unproven — he has run all five career starts over 6f, and if he ties up in the final two furlongs after setting the pace, the whole race shape unravels for horses who have tracked him.

Station Bar and Venturing are both true hold-up types forced into midfield by the crowded rear; watch whether jockeys Charles Bishop and William Carson attempt to push forward early, which could create minor positional friction behind Napolian in the first two furlongs.
Venturing returns from 132 days off with no turf or Good to Firm form — monitor market moves at the off; if weak in the market, the layoff concern is live and he is unlikely to be a factor.

Good to Firm ground is faster than the race headline states as "Good" — the official going report lists all Leicester races including this one as Good to Firm, so horses with a confirmed Good to Firm record (Pentonville, Station Bar) have a quiet edge over those with only AW or Soft form.

Albertini Star is a declared non-runner — confirm scratchings before finalising any race-shape assessment, as his removal reduces the field to six and slightly simplifies the hold-up traffic problem at the rear.
